newsitem.title: USA: NYC to appeal court ruling barring hospital deals.
newsitem.headline: NYC to appeal court ruling barring hospital deals.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani on Wednesday said that the city would appeal a court decision that bars his Administration from privatizing municipal hospitals.

The ruling by State Supreme Court Justice Herber Posner held state law would need to be changed before Giuliani could enter deals to privatize any of the 11 hospitals run by the city agency, Health and Hospitals Corp.

"We will appeal it," Giuliani told reporters, adding "I think there's a very good chance that it will be overturned on appeal." The mayor has been pushing to privatize city hospitals as way of saving money and providing better care.
The Health and Hospitals Corp, in a prepared statement, said "We believe the court's decision is erroneous, both on the facts and on the law."

The judge also held that the City Council has the right to review sales of city hospitals, which means that the Council would get to rule on a proposed 99-year lease of Coney Island Hospital in Brooklyn to PHS NEW YORK, a for-profit company tied to Primary Health Systems Inc of Wayne, PA.

The deal, which was reached late last year and which the city said would save it up to $100 million immediately, has been waiting for approval from state regulators, a process that can take 18 months or longer.

Alan Hevesi, the city comptroller, who has questioned whether the lease of the Coney Island hospital would produce the expected savings and provide adequate care for the poor, applauded the court's decision, saying it would require the Administration to hold a public review of the deal and the hospital agency.
